format: dashboard
---

```{r}
#| label: load-packages
#| include: false

library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(janitor)
library(lubridate)
```

```{r}
#| label: load-data
#| include: false

fd_customers    <- read.csv("../data/customers.csv")    |> clean_names()
fd_products     <- read.csv("../data/products.csv")     |> clean_names()
fd_transactions <- read.csv("../data/transactions.csv") |>
  clean_names() |>
  mutate(transaction_date = ymd(transaction_date))
fd_summary      <- read.csv("../data/customer_summary.csv") |> clean_names()

fd <- fd_transactions |>
  left_join(fd_customers, by = "customer_id") |>
  left_join(
    fd_products |> select(product_id, product_name, base_price),
    by = "product_id"
  )
```

```{r}
#| label: prep-data
#| include: false

# Revenue by category
revenue_by_cat <- fd |>
  group_by(category) |>
  summarise(total_revenue = sum(total_price, na.rm = TRUE)) |>
  arrange(desc(total_revenue)) |>
  mutate(category = factor(category, levels = category))

# Monthly revenue with trend (complete months only)
monthly_ts <- fd_transactions |>
  mutate(month_year = floor_date(transaction_date, "month")) |>
  filter(month_year < as.Date("2024-01-01")) |>
  group_by(month_year) |>
  summarise(monthly_revenue = sum(total_price, na.rm = TRUE)) |>
  mutate(
    t            = 1:n(),
    month_factor = as.factor(month(month_year))
  )

fd_ts_lm <- lm(monthly_revenue ~ t + month_factor, data = monthly_ts)
monthly_ts <- monthly_ts |>
  mutate(fitted = predict(fd_ts_lm, newdata = monthly_ts))

# Customer clusters
set.seed(5678)
fd_km <- fd_summary |> select(recency, frequency, monetary) |> scale()
km    <- kmeans(fd_km, centers = 3, nstart = 25)
fd_summary <- fd_summary |>
  mutate(cluster = as.factor(km$cluster))
```

# Revenue

## Row {height=100%}

### Column {width=50%}

```{r}
#| title: "Revenue by Product Category"

p <- ggplot(revenue_by_cat, aes(x = category, y = total_revenue))
p + geom_col(fill = "#6e0000") +
  labs(x = "Category", y = "Total Revenue ($)") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
```

**What this shows**: Total revenue by product category over the full 2022–2024 period. Electronics is the clear leader at ~$1.3M, followed by Home & Garden and Automotive. A business stakeholder should note the heavy concentration at the top — the bottom three categories combined generate less than Electronics alone.

### Column {width=50%}

```{r}
#| title: "Monthly Revenue Trend"

p <- ggplot(monthly_ts, aes(x = month_year, y = monthly_revenue))
p + geom_line(col = "navy") +
  geom_point(col = "navy", size = 1.5) +
  geom_line(aes(y = fitted), col = "maroon", linewidth = 1) +
  labs(x = "Month", y = "Revenue ($)") +
  scale_x_date(date_breaks = "3 months", date_labels = "%b %Y") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
```

**What this shows**: Actual monthly revenue (navy) alongside the fitted trend and seasonality model (maroon). Revenue grew roughly 18x from January 2022 to December 2023. The model (R² = 0.99) confirms a strong upward trend with July as the seasonal peak and February as the seasonal low each year.

# Customers

## Row {height=100%}

### Column {width=50%}

```{r}
#| title: "Customer Clusters by RFM"

p <- ggplot(fd_summary, aes(x = recency, y = monetary, col = cluster))
p + geom_point(alpha = 0.6) +
  scale_color_brewer("Cluster", palette = "Set1") +
  labs(x = "Recency (days since last purchase)", y = "Monetary Value ($)") +
  theme_bw()
```

**What this shows**: Each point is a customer, colored by segment. The high-value loyalists (Cluster 3) stand out with the highest spend; lapsed customers (Cluster 2) sit at the low end. A stakeholder should prioritize retaining Cluster 3 and re-engaging Cluster 2.

### Column {width=50%}

```{r}
#| title: "Purchase Frequency by Cluster"

p <- ggplot(fd_summary, aes(x = cluster, y = frequency, fill = cluster))
p + geom_boxplot(alpha = 0.7) +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set1") +
  labs(x = "Customer Cluster", y = "Purchase Frequency") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```

**What this shows**: Distribution of purchase frequency within each customer segment. Cluster 3 purchases most frequently (~8 orders on average), while Cluster 2 averages only ~2. The gap between segments signals a clear opportunity to move casual buyers toward higher engagement.
